subject: Post-call: Quickstart plan for SDKs, auth & routing (sample apps + local test)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Quickstart plan for SDKs, auth & routing (sample apps + local test)

Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation. This thread captures the technical next steps we agreed on and a short quickstart you can hand to your engineers to unblock a local pilot. High-level items below, followed by an attached quickstart bundle and checklist.

Recap (what we covered)
- Goal: embed model-powered product search + a conversational assistant for internal docs. Initial scope: embeddings for semantic search, generation for assistant with tool-calling for document fetch.
- Targets: POC in 2 weeks, local dev environment with sample apps (Python + TS) and CI smoke tests.
- Constraints: BrightPath will run pilot in AWS (us-west-2), and needs token encryption + audit logs.

Action items (owners & ETA)
1) Quickstart runbook + sample apps (Camila) — attached redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip. Steps for Python and TypeScript local runs. ETA: EOD Fri (2028-06-16).
2) Auth options doc and integration checklist (Marissa) — see integration-checklist.xlsx. We'll include KMS guidance and ephemeral keys. ETA: Mon (2028-06-18).
3) Routing & fallback diagram (Laura) — auth-routing-diagram.png attached. Shows model routing and canary fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained. ETA: Mon (2028-06-18).

Technical notes (for your engineers)
- SDKs: our Python and TypeScript packages demonstrate the same runtime APIs. Both examples show: init (api key/env var), streaming generation, embeddings client, and structured output parsing for tool-calling.
- Auth: recommended flow is short-lived API tokens issued via your Identity Provider -> Redwood Private mTLS or API gateway. Quickstart includes a simple env-var API key flow for local dev plus notes for exchanging with STS.
- Routing: sample config supports a primary model for low-latency queries and a cost-fallback model for heavy batch jobs. We include sample YAML route: by intent -> model, region -> region override.
- Embeddings & rerankers: quickstart has a small embedding pipeline (embedding, FAISS local index) and a fast reranker example (embedding similarity + light cross-encoder).

Questions / constraints you mentioned
- Audit logs + retention: we'll include guidance for sending request/response logs to your S3 bucket.
- Encryption in transit & at rest: use KMS for token encryption; we document HSM integration options.

Next sync
- Tentative tech drop-in Tue 6/19 10am PT to walk engineers through the ZIP. Please confirm who from your side will join.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (sample apps, README, local FAISS index seed), integration-checklist.xlsx, auth-routing-diagram.png

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our infra lead Anita:
- For the local pilot, can the quickstart run without any external cloud storage (purely local FAISS + sample data)? Anita prefers to validate the flows locally before we wire AWS S3/KMS.
- For auth, does the env-var key option require token rotation or will our engineers be able to swap in a short-lived token flow later without code changes?

We're targeting the 2-week POC but may compress if we can get a dev drop this week. I'm looping Anita so she can coordinate engineers for Tue 6/19.

Jordan

On Thu, Jun 14, 2028 at 9:12 AM Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation. This thread captures the technical next steps we agreed on and a short quickstart you can hand to your engineers to unblock a local pilot.

Jordan — quick answers:
- Yes, the quickstart is intentionally self-contained. The ZIP contains a seeded FAISS index and a small dataset so your team can run everything offline. No S3 required for the local dev flow.
- Env-var API key: that flow is a swap-in for convenience. The SDK supports an abstraction layer: credentials provider. In practice your engineers can implement short-lived token exchange (STS) without changing the higher-level call sites. We'll include a short snippet showing a credentials provider pattern in both Python and TS.

I attached a one-page checklist (integration-checklist.xlsx) that lists the exact files and env vars to change between local dev and your AWS pilot.

Camila — added a minor ask: can you include a short sample showing structured output + tool call (PDF fetch) in the README? BrightPath uses doc-retrieval heavily and they'd like to see tool-calling end-to-end.

Thanks,
Marissa

Where to find things:
- Quickstart ZIP (attached) — run: unzip && cd quickstart/python && pip install -r requirements.txt && python run_demo.py
- TS example: quickstart/ts -> npm install && npm run dev (local ENV flow documented)
- Structured output: quickstart/examples/tool_calling/README.md (includes sample prompt, schema, and sample code for post-processing tool responses)
